topics.label: Course introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series, outlining its structure, core themes, and specific learning outcomes.

topics.label: Cellular, genetic, and tissue foundations of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as a disease arising from accumulated genetic alterations, disrupted developmental differentiation, and altered tissue architecture studied in vivo and in vitro.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and tumor progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the histological and clinical distinctions between benign and malignant tumors, focusing on basement membrane invasion, metastatic routes, and the stepwise adenoma-to-carcinoma sequence.

topics.label: Neoplasm nomenclature and mechanisms of clinical morbidity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the standardized classification system for benign and malignant tumors alongside the physical and metabolic mechanisms by which they cause disease and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence across humans and animal taxa
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine epidemiological patterns of tumor frequency and mortality in human populations and compare cancer occurrence across diverse animal species.

topics.label: Principles and practice of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the clinical rationale for early cancer detection and evaluate the implementation and effectiveness of screening methods across various organ sites.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next steps
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reviewing learning outcomes and reminding students of upcoming practicals and lectures.
